quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 call, prepared remarks (President of Corporate Center Song Hyeon-jong): amid limited supply capabilities, SK Hynix expanded DRAM sales centered on HBM3E and AI server DRAM products; in particular, sales of LPDDR products for servers (including the module transcribed as 'SO-DIMM 2') grew significantly.

Q2 2026 call, prepared remarks (President Song Hyeon-jong): major big tech customers are expanding infrastructure investment due to increased AI service usage and a shortage of computing capacity, and 'our major customers are still requesting more memory supply'; on the supply side it 'appears difficult for the supply-demand balance to improve meaningfully in the near term' because of the growing complexity of advanced processes for HBM and AI server memory and the lead times to build new fabs, so tight conditions are expected to persist for a considerable period.

Q2 2026 call, Q&A (President Song Hyeon-jong, via interpreter): SK Hynix views big tech data-center leasing and more efficient AI models not as an AI investment slowdown but as higher utilization and accelerated monetization of infrastructure already built; it expects CSPs' AI-related investment to continue over the medium to long term and to 'remain solid beyond next year', though the timing of individual projects may differ due to physical constraints such as power availability and data center construction; it expects memory demand to expand across HBM, server DRAM for agentic AI and high-performance, high-capacity NAND.

Q2 2026 call, Q&A (management, via interpreter) on long-term agreements: the LTAs are designed in various forms per customer and product; the contract term is normally around five years, with specific conditions varying; pricing is not uniform, using a range of mechanisms to respond to price volatility; the agreements include long-term volume purchase commitments and mechanisms such as deposits; the company cannot say how much of total sales the LTAs will cover and intends to keep that share at an appropriate level to keep flexibility for incremental demand.
quarterly_data.figure: LTA contract term normally around five years

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 call, Q&A (management, via interpreter): in Q2 shipments of some high value-add products were pushed back into the second half and product-portfolio changes affected the blended DRAM ASP; management expects these factors to ease, with second-half bit growth higher than the first half as HBM4 shipments ramp in earnest and 1c-nanometer conventional DRAM shipments increase, and expects growing HBM4 sales and a higher value-add contribution to lift blended ASP and second-half earnings.

Q2 2026 call, Q&A (management, via interpreter) on HBM4 competitiveness: SK Hynix began mass production of HBM4 for key customers in Q2 with yield and quality 'nearing the levels of HBM3E', which is in the maturity stage; current focus is steadily ramping production capacity; HBM4E sample delivery to customers is completed, with development on roadmap 'aiming at volume production beginning in 2027'. Management cites time to market, performance, mass-production yield, quality and customer trust (demonstrated since HBM2E) as differentiators that cannot be replicated in a short period.
quarterly_data.figure: HBM4E volume production aimed to begin in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 call, Q&A (management, via interpreter): besides hybrid bonding, SK Hynix is developing iHBM technology (transcribed 'IHBM') for thermal dissipation in future products such as HBM5; iHBM integrates cooling elements within the package and is expected to reduce thermal resistance by more than 30%.
quarterly_data.figure: iHBM expected to reduce thermal resistance by more than 30%

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 call, Q&A (CFO Kim Woo-hyun, via interpreter): discussions on 2027 HBM supply volume and pricing with key customers are underway and progressing smoothly, supported by solid customer demand (terms not disclosed); the sharp rise in conventional DRAM prices 'may also have some influence' on HBM pricing talks, but HBM pricing is not set solely by conventional DRAM prices - it also reflects HBM's greater wafer input, advanced process, TSV and packaging capacity, technical complexity and the value delivered to customers.

Q2 2026 call, Q&A (President Song Hyeon-jong, via interpreter) on domestic vs overseas capacity: in Korea, Icheon and Yongin are to be the key production hubs for next-generation DRAM and AI memory, and Cheongju's capability is being strengthened for both NAND and advanced packaging; future production sites will be chosen on power, water, people, supply chain, ecosystem and customer accessibility rather than domestic vs overseas; at this time no further decisions on new production infrastructure have been made beyond the investments already announced.

contracts.signal: Q2 2026 call, Q&A (management, via interpreter): 'We have already built a solid base of profitability centered on HBM, supported by long-term collaborations with major AI customers like NVIDIA.'

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 call, prepared remarks: SK Hynix's enterprise SSD revenue increased twofold from the previous quarter, and Solidigm's revenue from high-capacity enterprise SSDs of 30 terabyte and above expanded more than threefold quarter-on-quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: enterprise SSD revenue up twofold QoQ; Solidigm 30 terabyte-and-above eSSD revenue up more than threefold QoQ

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 call, Q&A (Song Chang-seop, Head of NAND Marketing, via interpreter): as AI shifts from training to inference, NAND is becoming a core part of the AI memory hierarchy and eSSD-led NAND demand is expected to keep growing; SK Hynix's strategy is not a choice among SLC, TLC or QLC but a workload-optimized portfolio - high-capacity QLC eSSDs for AI data lakes and HDD replacement, high-performance TLC eSSDs and SLC-mode high-performance SSDs - and it is developing new-tier AI storage products for KV cache offloading and near-GPU storage.
